strongest_angle: Comparing the mythological combat feats, divine lineage, and distinct divine roles of Ares the war god and Hermes the messenger across classical sources like Theoi and Perseus.

key_facts.fact: Ares, the son of Zeus and Hera, is featured in classical myths including his capture by the Aloadai twins and conflicts with Herakles according to Theoi.
Hermes is credited in mythology with slaying the hundred-eyed giant Argos Panoptes and participating in the War of the Giants according to Theoi.
According to Harpers Dictionary of Classical Antiquities hosted at Perseus Tufts, Ares was the Greek god of war and son of Zeus and Heré.
Mythohub notes that Ares embodies the brutality of combat while Hermes represents speed, cunning, and commerce as the messenger of the gods.
